passages.text: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
Jehoshaphat had great riches.
Jehoshaphat had much honor.
Jehoshaphat made an alliance with Ahab.
Jehoshaphat joined Ahab by marriage.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֧י לִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֛ט עֹ֥שֶׁר וְכָב֖וֹד לָרֹ֑ב וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֖ן לְאַחְאָֽב׃

passages.text: And some years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria, where Ahab sacrificed many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him, and urged him to march up to Ramoth-gilead.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Ahab was the king of Israel.
After some years, Jehoshaphat went down to visit Ahab.
Ahab lived in Samaria.
Ahab sacrificed many sheep and cattle.
He did this for Jehoshaphat and for the people with him.
Ahab urged Jehoshaphat to go up to Ramoth-gilead.
passages.original: וַיֵּרֶד֩ לְקֵ֨ץ שָׁנִ֤ים אֶל־ אַחְאָב֙ לְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיִּֽזְבַּֽח־ ל֨וֹ אַחְאָ֜ב צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ לָרֹ֔ב וְלָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֑וֹ וַיְסִיתֵ֕הוּ לַעֲל֖וֹת אֶל־ רָמ֥וֹת גִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me against Ramoth-gilead?” And Jehoshaphat replied, “I am like you, and my people are your people; we will join you in the war.”
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Ahab spoke to Jehoshaphat.
Ahab asked, “Will you go with me to attack Ramoth-gilead?”
Jehoshaphat answered Ahab.
Jehoshaphat said, “I am like you.”
He said, “My people are your people.”
He said, “We will be with you in the war.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אַחְאָ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶל־ יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הֲתֵלֵ֥ךְ עִמִּ֖י רָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ כָּמ֤וֹנִי כָמ֙וֹךָ֙ וּכְעַמְּךָ֣ עַמִּ֔י וְעִמְּךָ֖ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: But Jehoshaphat also said to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for the word of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat spoke to Ahab.
Jehoshaphat said, “Let us ask for the word of the LORD today.”
Jehoshaphat wanted to hear God’s guidance before acting.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט אֶל־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דְּרָשׁ־ נָ֥א כַיּ֖וֹם אֶת־ דְּבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel assembled the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, “Should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up,” they replied, “and God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel gathered the prophets.
He brought together four hundred men.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead?”
He also asked, “Or should we not go?”
The prophets answered him.
They said, “Go up.”
They said, “God will give Ramoth-gilead into the king’s hand.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְבֹּ֨ץ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֶֽת־ הַנְּבִאִים֮ אַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֣וֹת אִישׁ֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל־ רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם־ אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ עֲלֵ֔ה וְיִתֵּ֥ן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not still a prophet of the LORD here of whom we can inquire?”
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
He spoke to the king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat asked a question.
He said, “Is there another prophet of the LORD here?”
He wanted to ask the LORD for guidance through that prophet.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט הַאֵ֨ין פֹּ֥ה נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה ע֑וֹד וְנִדְרְשָׁ֖ה מֵאֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The king of Israel answered, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.” “The king should not say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.
He said, “There is still one man who can ask the LORD for us.”
He said, “I hate him.”
He said, “He never prophesies anything good about me.”
He said, “He always prophesies bad things for me.”
He said, “His name is Micaiah son of Imlah.”
Jehoshaphat replied to the king.
Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say that.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל׀ אֶֽל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֡ט ע֣וֹד אִישׁ־ אֶחָ֡ד לִדְרוֹשׁ֩ אֶת־ יְהוָ֨ה מֵֽאֹת֜וֹ וַאֲנִ֣י שְׂנֵאתִ֗יהוּ כִּֽי־ אֵ֠ינֶנּוּ מִתְנַבֵּ֨א עָלַ֤י לְטוֹבָה֙ כִּ֣י כָל־ יָמָ֣יו לְרָעָ֔ה ה֖וּא מִיכָ֣יְהוּ בֶן־ יִמְלָ֑א וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יְה֣וֹשָׁפָ֔ט אַל־ יֹאמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke.
He called for one of his officials.
He gave a command to the official.
He said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־ סָרִ֖יס אֶחָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַהֵ֖ר מִיכָהוּ בֶן־ יִמְלָֽא׃

passages.text: Dressed in royal attire, the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel sat on his throne.
Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah, also sat on his throne.
Both kings wore royal clothes.
They sat at the threshing floor.
The threshing floor was by the entrance of the gate of Samaria.
All the prophets stood before them.
All the prophets prophesied in front of the two kings.
passages.original: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֡ה יוֹשְׁבִים֩ אִ֨ישׁ עַל־ כִּסְא֜וֹ מְלֻבָּשִׁ֤ים בְּגָדִים֙ וְיֹשְׁבִ֣ים בְּגֹ֔רֶן פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר שֹׁמְר֑וֹן וְכָל־ הַ֨נְּבִיאִ֔ים מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made for himself iron horns and declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are finished off.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was the son of Chenaanah.
He made iron horns for himself.
He spoke to the people.
He said, “This is what the LORD says.”
He said, “With these horns, you will gore the Arameans.”
He said, “You will do this until the Arameans are finished.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ ל֛וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ בֶֽן־ כְּנַעֲנָ֖ה קַרְנֵ֣י בַרְזֶ֑ל וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵ֛לֶּה תְּנַגַּ֥ח אֶת־ אֲרָ֖ם עַד־ כַּלּוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: And all the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for the LORD will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
passages.sermon:
All the prophets spoke together.
They all gave the same message.
They said, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead.
You will succeed.
The LORD will give the city into the king’s hand.”
passages.original: וְכָל־ הַ֨נְּבִאִ֔ים נִבְּאִ֥ים כֵּ֖ן לֵאמֹ֑ר עֲלֵ֞ה רָמֹ֤ת גִּלְעָד֙ וְהַצְלַ֔ח וְנָתַ֥ן יְהוָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah instructed him, “Behold, with one accord the words of the prophets are favorable to the king. So please let your words be like theirs, and speak favorably.”
passages.sermon:
A messenger went to call Micaiah.
This messenger spoke to Micaiah.
He said, “All the prophets speak together with one voice.
They speak good things to the king.
Let your words be like theirs.
Speak good things.”
passages.original: וְהַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ אֲשֶׁר־ הָלַ֣ךְ׀ לִקְרֹ֣א לְמִיכָ֗יְהוּ דִּבֶּ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֞ה דִּבְרֵ֧י הַנְּבִאִ֛ים פֶּֽה־ אֶחָ֥ד ט֖וֹב אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וִֽיהִי־ נָ֧א דְבָרְךָ֛ כְּאַחַ֥ד מֵהֶ֖ם וְדִבַּ֥רְתָּ טּֽוֹב׃

passages.text: But Micaiah said, “As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever my God tells me.”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to the messenger.
Micaiah said, "The LORD lives."
Micaiah said, "I will speak only what my God tells me."
Micaiah promised to say only God's words.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִיכָ֑יְהוּ חַי־ יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֛י אֶת־ אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאמַ֥ר אֱלֹהַ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: When Micaiah arrived, the king asked him, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” “Go up and triumph,” Micaiah replied, “for they will be given into your hand.”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah came to the king.
The king spoke to Micaiah.
The king asked, “Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead?”
The king also asked, “Or should we not go?”
Micaiah answered the king.
Micaiah said, “Go up.”
Micaiah said, “Succeed.”
Micaiah said, “They will be given into your hand.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֮ אֶל־ הַמֶּלֶךְ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֵלָ֗יו מִיכָה֙ הֲנֵלֵ֞ךְ אֶל־ רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָ֛ד לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אִם־ אֶחְדָּ֑ל וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ עֲל֣וּ וְהַצְלִ֔יחוּ וְיִנָּתְנ֖וּ בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to Micaiah.
The king said, “How many times must I make you swear?”
The king wanted Micaiah to speak only the truth.
The king said, “Do not tell me anything except the truth.”
The king said, “Speak in the name of the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַד־ כַּמֶּ֥ה פְעָמִ֖ים אֲנִ֣י מַשְׁבִּיעֶ֑ךָ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־ תְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י רַק־ אֱמֶ֖ת בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So Micaiah declared: “I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These people have no master; let each one return home in peace.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet.
Micaiah spoke to the king.
Micaiah said, “I saw all Israel.”
The people of Israel were scattered on the hills.
They were like sheep without a shepherd.
The LORD spoke.
The LORD said, “These people have no master.”
The LORD said, “Let each one return to his home in peace.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְפוֹצִ֣ים עַל־ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים כַּצֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־ לָהֶ֖ן רֹעֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ לֹֽא־ אֲדֹנִ֣ים לָאֵ֔לֶּה יָשׁ֥וּבוּ אִישׁ־ לְבֵית֖וֹ בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he never prophesies good for me, but only bad?”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.
He said, “Did I not tell you this before?”
He said, “He never prophesies good for me.”
He only prophesies bad for me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֑ט הֲלֹא֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ לֹא־ יִתְנַבֵּ֥א עָלַ֛י ט֖וֹב כִּ֥י אִם־ לְרָֽע׃ס

passages.text: Micaiah continued, “Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right and on His left.
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to the people.
Micaiah said, "Listen to the word of the LORD."
Micaiah saw a vision.
Micaiah saw the LORD.
The LORD was sitting on His throne.
The host of heaven stood around the LORD.
Some stood on the LORD’s right side.
Some stood on the LORD’s left side.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֑ה רָאִ֤יתִי אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב עַל־ כִּסְא֔וֹ וְכָל־ צְבָ֤א הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ עֹֽמְדִ֔ים עַל־ יְמִינ֖וֹ וּשְׂמֹאלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And the LORD said, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ And one suggested this, and another that.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Ahab is the king of Israel.
The LORD asked a question.
The LORD said, “Who will entice Ahab?”
The LORD wanted Ahab to go up to Ramoth-gilead.
The LORD wanted Ahab to fall there.
One being answered with one idea.
Another being answered with a different idea.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה מִ֤י יְפַתֶּה֙ אֶת־ אַחְאָ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַ֕עַל וְיִפֹּ֖ל בְּרָמ֣וֹת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֶ֚ה אֹמֵ֣ר כָּ֔כָה וְזֶ֖ה אֹמֵ֥ר כָּֽכָה׃

passages.text: Then a spirit came forward, stood before the LORD, and said, ‘I will entice him.’ ‘By what means?’ asked the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A spirit came forward.
The spirit stood before the LORD.
The spirit said, “I will entice him.”
The LORD asked the spirit, “By what means?”
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֣א הָר֗וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲנִ֣י אֲפַתֶּ֑נּוּ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו בַּמָּֽה׃

passages.text: And he replied, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ ‘You will surely entice him and prevail,’ said the LORD. ‘Go and do it.’
passages.sermon:
A spirit stood before the LORD.
The spirit spoke to the LORD.
The spirit said, “I will go out.”
The spirit said, “I will become a lying spirit.”
The spirit said, “I will be in the mouths of all Ahab’s prophets.”
The LORD answered the spirit.
The LORD said, “You will entice Ahab.”
The LORD said, “You will succeed.”
The LORD said, “Go.”
The LORD said, “Do this.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵצֵא֙ וְהָיִ֙יתִי֙ לְר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י כָּל־ נְבִיאָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּפַתֶּה֙ וְגַם־ תּוּכָ֔ל צֵ֖א וַעֲשֵׂה־ כֵֽן׃

passages.text: So you see, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours, and the LORD has pronounced disaster against you.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD has power over spirits.
The LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of your prophets.
These prophets are your prophets.
The LORD has spoken disaster against you.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ ר֣וּחַ שֶׁ֔קֶר בְּפִ֖י נְבִיאֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ רָעָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah went up, struck Micaiah in the face, and demanded, “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He departed from me to speak with you?”
passages.sermon:
Zedekiah was the son of Chenaanah.
He went up to Micaiah.
Zedekiah struck Micaiah on the face.
Zedekiah spoke to Micaiah.
He asked Micaiah a question.
Zedekiah said, “Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He left me to speak with you?”
passages.original: וַיִּגַּשׁ֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בֶֽן־ כְּנַעֲנָ֔ה וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־ מִיכָ֖יְהוּ עַל־ הַלֶּ֑חִי וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣י זֶ֤ה הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ עָבַ֧ר רֽוּחַ־ יְהוָ֛ה מֵאִתִּ֖י לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֹתָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Micaiah replied, “You will soon see, on that day when you go and hide in an inner room.”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah struck Micaiah in the face.
Zedekiah asked Micaiah a question about the Spirit of the LORD.
Micaiah replied to Zedekiah.
Micaiah said, “You will see the truth on that day.
On that day, you will go into an inner room.
You will hide there.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ הִנְּךָ֥ רֹאֶ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּב֛וֹא חֶ֥דֶר בְּחֶ֖דֶר לְהֵחָבֵֽא׃

passages.text: And the king of Israel declared, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king’s son, and tell them that this is what the king says: ‘Put this man in prison and feed him only bread and water until I return safely.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke.
He gave a command.
He said, “Take Micaiah.”
He said, “Return him to Amon.”
Amon was the governor of the city.
He also said, “Return him to Joash.”
Joash was the king’s son.
The king gave further instructions.
He said, “Tell them this is what the king says.”
He said, “Put this man in prison.”
He said, “Feed him only bread and water.”
He said, “Do this until I return safely.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל קְחוּ֙ אֶת־ מִיכָ֔יְהוּ וַהֲשִׁיבֻ֖הוּ אֶל־ אָמ֣וֹן שַׂר־ הָעִ֑יר וְאֶל־ יוֹאָ֖שׁ בֶּן־ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שִׂ֥ימוּ זֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית הַכֶּ֑לֶא וְהַאֲכִלֻ֜הוּ לֶ֤חֶם לַ֙חַץ֙ וּמַ֣יִם לַ֔חַץ עַ֖ד שׁוּבִ֥י בְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: But Micaiah replied, “If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me.” Then he added, “Take heed, all you people!”
passages.sermon:
Micaiah was a prophet of the LORD.
Micaiah spoke to the king of Israel.
Micaiah said, "If you return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me."
Micaiah then spoke to all the people.
Micaiah said, "Listen, all you people."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מִיכָ֔יְהוּ אִם־ שׁ֤וֹב תָּשׁוּב֙ בְּשָׁל֔וֹם לֹא־ דִבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁמְע֖וּ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃פ

passages.text: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel was a ruler over Israel.
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat went together.
They went up to Ramoth-gilead.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַל מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וִֽיהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל־ רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד׃

passages.text: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat.
The king of Israel said, "I will disguise myself and go into battle."
The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "You wear your royal robes."
The king of Israel disguised himself.
The king of Israel went into battle.
Jehoshaphat wore his royal robes.
They both went into battle.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט הִתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ וָב֣וֹא בַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְאַתָּ֖ה לְבַ֣שׁ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ וַיִּתְחַפֵּשׂ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Now the king of Aram had ordered his chariot commanders, “Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The king of Aram gave an order to his chariot commanders.
He told them what to do in battle.
He said, “Do not fight anyone else.
Do not fight the small or the great.
Fight only the king of Israel.”
passages.original: וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֡ם צִוָּה֩ אֶת־ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֤כֶב אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֚א תִּלָּ֣חֲמ֔וּ אֶת־ הַקָּטֹ֖ן אֶת־ הַגָּד֑וֹל כִּ֛י אִֽם־ אֶת־ מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “This is the king of Israel!” So they turned to fight against him, but Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.
passages.sermon:
Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah.
The chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat.
They thought he was the king of Israel.
They said, “This is the king of Israel.”
They turned to fight against Jehoshaphat.
Jehoshaphat cried out.
The LORD helped Jehoshaphat.
God caused the chariot commanders to turn away from Jehoshaphat.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י כִּרְאוֹת֩ שָׂרֵ֨י הָרֶ֜כֶב אֶת־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט וְהֵ֤מָּה אָֽמְרוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ה֔וּא וַיָּסֹ֥בּוּ עָלָ֖יו לְהִלָּחֵ֑ם וַיִּזְעַ֤ק יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ וַֽיהוָ֣ה עֲזָר֔וֹ וַיְסִיתֵ֥ם אֱלֹהִ֖ים מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: And when the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
passages.sermon:
The chariot commanders served the king of Aram.
They looked at Jehoshaphat.
They realized he was not the king of Israel.
They stopped chasing him.
They turned away from him.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְאוֹת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב כִּ֥י לֹא־ הָיָ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ מֵאַחֲרָֽיו׃

passages.text: However, a certain man drew his bow without taking special aim, and he struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So the king said to his charioteer, “Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am badly wounded!”
passages.sermon:
A man drew his bow.
He did not aim at anyone in particular.
He shot an arrow.
The arrow struck the king of Israel.
It hit him between the joints of his armor.
The king of Israel was wounded.
He spoke to his chariot driver.
He said, "Turn your hands."
He said, "Take me out of the battle."
He said, "I am badly wounded."
passages.original: וְאִ֗ישׁ מָשַׁ֤ךְ בַּקֶּ֙שֶׁת֙ לְתֻמּ֔וֹ וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בֵּ֥ין הַדְּבָקִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ין הַשִּׁרְיָ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָֽרַכָּ֗ב הֲפֹ֧ךְ יָדֶיךָ וְהוֹצֵאתַ֥נִי מִן־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה כִּ֥י הָחֳלֵֽיתִי׃

passages.text: The battle raged throughout that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. And at sunset he died.
passages.sermon:
The king of Israel fought in a battle against the Arameans.
The battle continued all day.
The king of Israel stayed in his chariot.
He faced the Arameans until evening.
At sunset, the king of Israel died.
passages.original: וַתַּ֤עַל הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וּמֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הָיָ֨ה מַעֲמִ֧יד בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה נֹ֥כַח אֲרָ֖ם עַד־ הָעָ֑רֶב וַיָּ֕מָת לְעֵ֖ת בּ֥וֹא הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
